body:
Triage (finding round): promoted → `pm:queue`, `domain:services` (service-messaging + plugin-webhooks), type Bug. The two classifications are the dispatch clauses, verbatim from the card: `ack` × 2 inherit #10673's documented structural sweep warrant; **`redeliver` threads the request's tenant and must NEVER get `bypassTenantAudit`** — it is request-reachable by any authenticated user, so on an isolated posture it is exactly the unscoped write the audit exists to catch. Threading the tenant narrows accepted writes back to the declared tenancy invariant (not a product decision), but it changes `IHttpOutbox.redeliver`'s signature: claim with `Clause-②: yes` and the contract-review tier. Re-measure by driving a real delivery through, not by reading a boot log — the card's own warning.

PR stays **draft**; `needs:contract-review` hung as the compensating control. ⛔ This seat does not clear it.
- serial constraint: `packages/services/service-messaging` (`sql-http-outbox.ts`, `sql-outbox.ts`) and `outbox-dispatcher-scope.ts`. Free.

## Why this is dispatchable when it says "needs a contract decision"

Because the decision is already made **against** the wrong answer, and the card makes it:

> ⛔ It must not be given `bypassTenantAudit` to make the line go away — the audit's whole purpose is to force this classification, and this is the site it was built for.

What remains is implementing the named remedy — thread the request's tenant — at the tier that change earns. That is work, not a ruling. ⛔ If the implementation turns up a reason the tenant **cannot** be threaded, that is a `needs_decision` and it comes back; it is not licence to fall back to a bypass.

## ⛔ The one mistake that must not be made

The three sites are on one object and their classifications are **opposite**. Treating this as one sweep is the dangerous error:

| site | reachable from | classification |
|---|---|---|
| `SqlNotificationOutbox.ack` | dispatcher tick only | global sweep — inherits #10673's structural warrant |
| `SqlHttpOutbox.ack` | dispatcher tick only | global sweep — same warrant |
| **`SqlHttpOutbox.redeliver`** | **`POST /api/v1/webhooks/redeliver`** | ⛔ **request-contextual** |

`plugin-webhooks`' own comment on that route says **any authenticated user can reach it**. Under `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated` that is an unscoped write reachable by an authenticated user — the exact case the tenant audit exists to catch, and the one case where silencing the line converts a **detectable** hole into an **undetectable** one.

The two `ack` sites earn their warrant **structurally**, not by judgement: their only callers are the dispatchers' `setInterval` tick under a cluster lock; `ClaimOptions` / `HttpClaimOptions` carry no tenant **even in principle**; partitioning is `hash(...) mod N` — a load-spreading key, not an org key, so a partition holds every org's rows by construction; and one outbox per environment drains the whole queue, so a per-org predicate would strand every other org's deliveries and leave a crashed node's rows permanently `in_flight`. **Re-derive that warrant rather than inheriting it** — if any limb of it no longer holds, the classification changes.

⚠️ `outbox-dispatcher-scope.ts` (added by PR #10725) already holds the reasoning, but its return type is `& { multi: true }`, so **it cannot be reused here as-is — and that is deliberate.** These are `multi: false` sites under the `update` op, a different op from the `updateMany` one #10673 covered.

## ⚠️ Do not re-measure this from a boot log

#10673's card quotes a composed-boot startup log showing exactly two `[tenant-audit]` lines. That is **not** evidence the `update` op is clean, and the card says why:

> The reap `UPDATE` runs unconditionally on every dispatcher tick, while `ack` / `redeliver` only run once a delivery is **actually processed**. A startup log taken on an empty queue therefore shows exactly the two `updateMany` lines and says nothing at all about the `update`-op surface.

**Drive an actual delivery through.** An audit line that does not appear because nothing ran is NOT MEASURED, not a pass — the same class as a gate that refuses.

## Pins — both directions

- `redeliver` carries the caller's tenant, and the audit line for that site **disappears because the write is scoped**, not because it was silenced. Prove the distinction: a scoped write and a bypassed write both produce no audit line, so an assertion that only checks for the line's absence cannot tell them apart. Assert the predicate that reached the driver.
- the two `ack` sites still audit-clean under their warrant, and a delivery actually flows.
- **a cross-tenant `redeliver` attempt is refused**, with ADR-0112 `code` **AND** `status`.
- **still-works**: an in-tenant redeliver still succeeds. An implementation that refuses every redeliver would pass a one-directional suite.

## Standing proof standard

Ablation with the signature predicted **first**; restore proved byte-identical by `git hash-object`. Prove `src/` vs `dist/` resolution argued from the files. Zero-hit counter-check with a positive control on the same corpus — and note that a *non-zero* from a term that pre-dates your change proves nothing either. Gate union derived on the **final** commit, clean tree, `dispatch-gates.mjs` with **no path arguments**, exit codes captured before any pipe. Class #10309 is live — run what you judge relevant explicitly and say whether the derivation named it. Changeset required. Never `git stash` (shared stack). Never report a grep hit count as a fact count.

⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/**`. ⛔ Zero `packages/spec` ownership in this lane — if the contract change needs a spec edit, **stop and report**; it carves out like #10999 did.

⚠️ Not in scope: cloud#1512's `crm_contract` half. Do not reach for it.

## Refs

#10673 / PR #10725 (the `updateMany` half and the structural warrant) · `sql-http-outbox.ts`, `sql-outbox.ts` · `sql-driver.ts` `auditMissingTenant` (the instrument) · cloud#1512 (upstream)

## Contract review — PASS (clause ②)

Reviewing seat: skills PM (`session_01ApyDuQY2fkunMCqXiqvBhR`), machine-verified at tier this round (`get_session` → `external_metadata.last_served_model = claude-fable-5` = `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on `origin/main`). Not the dispatching seat.

Scope reviewed: the contract-face increment of draft PR #11010 at `1091f1e60`, from the actual diff (15 files) — the interface, the service delegate, the SQL implementation, the route, the helper, and the changeset were each read; the rest sampled.

**Findings, checked against the diff:**

1. **The signature shape is the right kind of forced.** `RedeliverOptions.tenantId` is required and typed `string | undefined`, so the dangerous case — a request path that simply forgot — cannot compile, while a genuinely tenant-less caller must write `tenantId: undefined` and mean it. The report's typecheck evidence (10 errors across 4 files on first compile after the change) is this design working as the notification channel.
2. **Cross-tenant behavior is invisible, not forbidden — deliberately.** The scope is threaded to both reads and the write from one shared options bag, so the refusal surfaces as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` and the endpoint is not an existence oracle for other tenants' delivery ids; the producer guard never sees a row the caller may not read. In-tenant redelivery unchanged (still-works pinned).
3. **Zero `bypassTenantAudit` on the redeliver path**, verified in the diff and backed by the report's zero-hit counter-check with positive control. The scoped-vs-bypassed distinction is asserted at the driver (a spy on the one method that both audits and scopes), which is the only place the two are distinguishable — and the "tenant-less caller is NOT silenced" test makes a future bypass go red rather than green.
4. **The two `ack` sites get their own helper, not a borrowed warrant.** `dispatcherAckOptions()` is `multi: false` by type so the sweep helper cannot be confused for it, all four warrant limbs were re-derived on this tree, and the docblock names the tempting wrong answer (stamping the claimed row's own `organization_id` — a tautological predicate that silences the audit while adding no isolation) and why it is worse than the declared bypass. This is exactly the classification discipline the card demanded.
5. **Route-side tenant resolution is single-sourced.** `session.session.activeOrganizationId`, read from the canonical spelling with no `??` chain over alternatives — so a missing organization stays visible (threads `undefined`, audit fires) instead of being papered over. One `getSession` lookup serves both the auth gate and the tenant, so they cannot disagree.
6. **Changeset and ADR-0087 handling are honest.** BREAKING signature change shipped `minor` per the repo's launch-window convention; the `adr-0087: not-required (runtime-interface-only …)` marker names exactly the two symbols the gate can resolve (`IHttpOutbox`, `RedeliverOptions`) and states the `MessagingService.redeliverHttp` claim in prose because the gate refuses that symbol as unresolvable — claiming it where a checker would appear to have verified it would be worse. Flagged as a judgment call by the seat; upheld here.
7. **`MemoryHttpOutbox` accepting-and-ignoring `tenantId` is documented in place** with the reason (no tenant column, test/dev double) and the obligation on any future tenant-storing memory implementation. Acceptable.

Noted, not blocking: the seat's out-of-scope finding #11009 (a compare-and-set `where` on a by-id `update` is silently inert at the SQL driver) means redeliver's `status: $in` guard predicate does not currently bind at the driver — pre-existing, correctly filed separately, and this PR's read-back check (`after.status !== 'pending'` → `DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE`) is what actually holds that line today.

**Verdict: PASS.** `needs:contract-review` cleared (four-step read-modify-write with read-back; label was issue-side only — PR #11010 carries none). Ready-flipping stays with the dispatching seat.
